Content of the OpenVPN configuration file. These files are usually have the extension .ovpn (sometimes also .conf) and are plain text multi line configuration files. If your MDM does not support multiline configuration entries, you can also use a base64 encoded string here. A text file can be converted to base64 using openssl base64 -A -in
Alias of a certificate in the Android keystore to use. Leave empty to not use the certificate store.
Version of the managed configuration schema (Currently always 1)
UUID of the profile that should be selected as default profile in the app

CentVPN does not communicate with any server other than the OpenVPN servers defined in your configuration files, apart from two optional features that are off by default and that you explicitly control.

Country display: if you enable it, the app queries the third-party geolocation service api.country.is to show your current public IP address and country. Only your public IP address is sent, and the response (IP and country code) is stored locally on your device.

Free public servers: if you enable it, the app downloads the public VPN server list from the VPNGate project (vpngate.net) so you can browse and import free community servers. This is only a download of that public list and sends no personal data.

The author operates no backend, collects no data, and therefore stores no data.

For the privacy policies of the OpenVPN server / VPN service you use, api.country.is, vpngate.net, or other services related to the project such as GitHub, please refer to their respective privacy policies.
